title: Bangkok 3D — Interactive Urban Tourist Guide & Explorer Studio
description: A complete, self-contained interactive 3D tourist guide to Bangkok built in vanilla HTML5, CSS3 and ES6 with Three.js r128. It renders a compressed Rattanakosin city around the Chao Phraya with five hand-built landmarks — Wat Arun, Wat Pho, the Grand Palace, the Golden Mount and Baiyoke Tower II — plus procedural blocks, roads, bridges, parks, traffic, boats, river shaders and floating markers. Three camera modes (OrbitControls drone, drag-to-look street walk with collision, scroll zoom and footsteps, and an automated Catmull-Rom transit tour with five dwell stops), bilingual English/Thai copy and narration, midday/golden-hour/neon-night lighting, synthesised spatial Web Audio ambience, a live minimap, and localStorage plus JSON itinerary export/import.

build.includes: Project scaffold; renderer, sky shader, stars, sun and moon; sRGB-correct materials and eight procedural facade texture sets; Chao Phraya river with animated water shader, embankments, promenade, railings and lamps; road grid, lane markings, crossings, two bridges, parks, ponds, trees, street lamps and instanced traffic; five procedural landmark models (Wat Arun prangs and porcelain bands; Wat Pho ubosot, four chedis and open-canopy Reclining Buddha; Grand Palace crenellated walls, Wat Phra Kaew, golden chedi and Chakri Maha Prasat; Golden Mount terraced hill with spiral path and gold chedi; Baiyoke glass tower with observation crown, neon and beacon); five bobbing 3D markers and pick volumes; drone, first-person walk with collision, sprint, head bob and footsteps, and a five-stop spline transit tour; EN/TH UI and landmark copy; three lighting presets with smooth transitions; spatial Web Audio synthesis and speech narration; minimap; visited stamps, route builder and notes; localStorage autosave; JSON export/import as bangkok_3d_tour.json; 24-check self-test; responsive mobile layout; documentation, licence, notices, robots, sitemap and GitHub Pages deployment.

notes: All geometry, textures, audio and copy are original; no photographs, map tiles or external models are redistributed.
Geography is deliberately compressed and interpretive, not survey data.
Fees and hours are a 2026 travel-guide snapshot and are not fetched live.
Walk mode uses keyboard movement and mouse drag to look; the walkable area is the east bank.
The final GitHub Pages deployment is verified after this snapshot.

revisions.summary: Post-publish controls revision: removed pointer-lock mouse capture; walk mode now uses ordinary drag-to-look with scroll-wheel field-of-view zoom. Tour also supports scroll-wheel zoom. Self-test grew from 23 to 24 checks (drag-look + zoom).

Documentation release: added changelog, contribution/security/support policies, architecture, controls, data-format, testing, deployment, accessibility, performance, FAQ, roadmap and release-checklist docs; added GitHub issue/PR templates and a static CI check. App version moved to 1.1.0.
Patch: inverted horizontal walk drag so dragging left reveals the right side of the landscape. Vertical look and zoom unchanged. Version 1.1.1.
Patch: restored reliable walking after guide/notes interaction by returning focus to the scene; arrow keys now prevent page scroll and are presented alongside WASD. Version 1.1.2.
Patch: added a mouse/touch on-screen walk pad; restricted walk-mode picking to marker meshes only; local CSS/JS cache-busting; walking is keyboard-optional. Version 1.1.3.
Feature: replaced box traffic with layered low-poly cars (tapered body, glass cabin, roof, four wheels, head/tail lights) using six instanced meshes. Version 1.2.0.

Documentation: added privacy policy, browser-support matrix, design language, screenshot gallery, Thai glossary and CITATION.cff; linked them from README, docs index, AGENTS and deployment records. No runtime change; version remains 1.2.0.
